studies_list.title: Effects of six weeks of guanidinoacetic acid supplementation with and without creatine monohydrate on cognitive function and markers of health in healthy adults.
studies_list.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

s3.population_text: Apparently healthy or medically controlled males and females 18-65 years; excluded pregnancy/breastfeeding, cognitive impairment, neurological disease.
evidence_spans: PLA (PLA, 2 × 6 g/d maltodextrin), GAA (2 × 1 g/d) + PLA (2 × 5 g/d), or GAA (2 × 1 g/d) + CrM (2 × 5 g/d) for six weeks
20 individuals (12 females, 8 males) were randomized into treatment A (GAA + CrM group), 19 individuals ... treatment B (GAA group), and 19 participants ... treatment C (PLA group)
apparently healthy or medically controlled males and females between 18 and 65 years of age
randomized, counterbalanced, double-blind, placebo-controlled
the participants were matched based on sex, age, and weight and randomly assigned in a counterbalanced manner
Supplements were distributed to participants in generic stick packets... labeled "A," "B," or "C," for double-blind administration
This trial was registered in the International Standard Randomized Controlled Trial Number (ISRCTN) registry (#68542582, posted November 12, 2025)
This study was approved by the University Human Research Protection Program Internal Review Board (IRB2024-1370, approved January 10, 2025)
Randomized and Initiated with n equals 58
Analyzed boxes...n equals 20...n equals 19...n equals 19
No participant withdrew from the study because of issues with the supplement

studies_list.title: Effects of creatine supplementation with and without exercise and diet intervention on body composition, cognitive function, and markers of health in middle-aged and older adults.
studies_list.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

s3.population_text: Healthy, community-dwelling adults aged 45-65, apparently healthy or medically stable
evidence_spans: randomized...to 2 × 5 g/d of maltodextrin placebo (PLA) or CrM
Sixty-four adults aged 45–65 years...completed the 12-week intervention
NoEx+CrM...NoEx+PLA...Ex+CrM...Ex+PLA
Allocation included 16...PLA, 15...CrM, 21...Ex+PLA, 21...Ex+CrM
randomly assigned in a counterbalanced manner to CrM or PLA
Participants and study personnel remained blinded to supplement assignment until the database was finalized
Placebo supplements consisted of maltodextrin
The first participant was enrolled on July 10, 2024. The trial was submitted to the ISRCTN registry on April 11, 2025
Fifteen individuals declined participation due to time constraints... Injury/illness n=2, COVID-19 n=1
The repeated-measures GLM included the 64 participants who completed the 12-week intervention
Seventy-three participants selected exercise or non-exercise participation and were then... randomized
Sixty-four adults...completed the 12-week intervention and were analyzed

s5_claims.evidence_span: significant interaction effects seen in fat mass... fat-free mass (p = 0.016)... Participants in the CrM supplemented groups gained fat-free mass compared to the NoEx+PLA and Ex+PLA groups

claim.evidence_span: Participants in the CrM supplemented groups gained fat-free mass compared to the NoEx+PLA and Ex+PLA groups

s5_claims.evidence_span: percentage body fat loss was statistically significantly greater in the Ex+CrM than NoEx+PLA, NoEx+CrM and Ex+PLA groups
statistically significant interaction effects seen in fat mass (p = 0.007... group × time (p = 0.037)

claim.evidence_span: overall reaction times increased in the Ex+PLA and Ex+CrM groups while being unchanged in the NoEx+PLA and NoEx+CrM groups. The number of false alarms identified tended to increase in the Ex+CrM group

Additionally, no statistically significant differences were observed in mean change from baseline analysis (see Figure 13).

claim.outcome_raw: Light reaction test (move time, reaction time, etc.)
claim.evidence_span: Average and best scores on the light reaction test are presented in Tables S17 and S18, respectively. No statistically significant multivariate or univariate effects were observed in move time, start speed, targets correctly identified, consistency score, total scores, total time, fastest successful trial, lowest missed trial, or reaction time scores.
